title: Number of Beautiful Pairs
summary: Given an integer array nums, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < nums.length, such that the first digit of nums[i] and the last digit of nums[j] are coprime.
statement: Given an integer array nums, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < nums.length, such that the first digit of nums[i] and the last digit of nums[j] are coprime. Two numbers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is 1.
constraints: For every index pair i<j, take the first decimal digit of nums[i] and last digit of nums[j].
The pair is beautiful when those digits have greatest common divisor one.
Return the number of beautiful pairs.
reference_solution:
def count_beautiful_digit_pairs(nums):
    from math import gcd
    first_counts=[0]*10;answer=0
    for value in nums:
        last=value%10;answer+=sum(first_counts[digit] for digit in range(1,10) if gcd(digit,last)==1)
        first_counts[int(str(value)[0])]+=1
    return answer

Scan left to right; before storing the current first digit, compare its last digit with earlier first-digit counts.
Add counts for digits whose gcd with the current last digit is one.
At index j the table represents exactly all eligible earlier i values, so every ordered index pair is tested once.
